title: What Transliteration Preserves
excerpt: On the relationship between source script, romanized text, and the details that must survive the journey between them.
body:
Transliteration represents one writing system through another. Its purpose is not to change the language, but to give readers a consistent path into its written form.

Why consistency matters

A useful transliteration system makes its conventions visible. Readers should be able to see how letters, marks, or sounds in the source are represented in the romanized text.

Good transliteration keeps the reader close to the structure of the source.

Precision and readability need not be opposites. The best editorial choices explain what is preserved, what is normalized, and where uncertainty remains.

title: Building a Digital Text Archive
excerpt: Practical notes on organizing texts so they can be browsed, searched, cited, illustrated, and updated over time.
body:
A digital archive is most useful when every text carries enough context to stand on its own.

A durable record

Each entry should include a clear title, language, source note, date, editorial status, and an image when one is available. Together these details make the collection useful to both casual readers and researchers.

Designed to grow

This website stores entries in a simple open format. The collection can be backed up, moved, or extended without dependence on a proprietary publishing platform.
